fields.summary: Complex obs storage abstraction performs redundant exists/metadata calls per read
fields.description:
h2. Background

The 2.8.x storage-service abstraction for complex obs changed {{AbstractHandler.getObs()}} from a single file read into: a {{storageService.exists()}} probe (to distinguish legacy vs. new key layouts), the {{getData()}} read, and a separate {{getMetadata()}} call — with {{LocalStorageService.getPath()}} adding a further legacy-path existence check per call. On local storage this turns one file open into ~4–5 filesystem operations; on S3-backed storage a single complex obs view costs three network round-trips (HEAD/GET/HEAD) where 2.6.x performed one local read. This applies to all bundled handlers (Image, Binary, Text, Media, BinaryStream).

h2. Requested change

Reduce per-read storage operations: resolve the legacy-vs-new key layout without a separate existence probe where possible (or cache the resolution), and fetch data and metadata in a single operation when the backend supports it (e.g. S3 GetObject already returns metadata). Behavior for both legacy and new key layouts must be preserved.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Reading a complex obs performs at most one existence-related check and does not issue a separate metadata request when the data request already provides it.
* Legacy-layout obs continue to load correctly (covered by tests for both layouts).
* Unit tests assert the number of storage-service calls per {{getObs()}} for local storage, preventing reintroduction of redundant probes.
